The question was matched to: microgravity, diffusion flame. Below is what the indexed documents state about it, quoted with their sources.

**Evidence**
- ACME CFI-G: ACME CFI-G Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Cool Flames Investigation with Gases. Flames of Gaseous Fuels. ACME, Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) [S1]
- ACME CLD Flame: ACME CLD Flame Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame. Flames of gaseous fuel. Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME [S2]
- SLICE: Liftoff and stabilisation of jet flames in co-flow — how flames anchor or blow off. [S3]
- ACME s-Flame: ACME s-Flame Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments-Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames. Flames of gaseous fuels. Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME [S4]
- SPICE: (1) Identify the laminar smoke-point properties of non-buoyant jet diffusion flames under various co-flow conditions in microgravity. [S5]
- Dust can look like smoke to a particle counter: DAFT showed that a modified commercial particle counter could be used in microgravity, measuring a test dust aerosol released on the ISS. Limitation: Terrestrial test dust, not lunar regolith; feasibility test only. [S10]
- Cool flames: combustion at 500–1000 K: Cool diffusion flames have peak temperatures of about 500–1000 K. FLEX, CFI and CFI-G studied them on droplets and burners in microgravity. Limitation: Research fuels and configurations; relevance to cabin fires is an open question, not a f [S11]

- Only documents in this knowledge base were searched.

sources.title: Cool flames: combustion at 500–1000 K
sources.text: Cool diffusion flames have peak temperatures of about 500–1000 K. FLEX, CFI and CFI-G studied them on droplets and burners in microgravity. Limitation: Research fuels and configurations; relevance to cabin fires is an open question, not a finding.

sources.title: More oxygen: droplet flames more often survive to burnout
sources.text: FLEX droplet tests in N2-only atmospheres that ended in flame extinction before burnout — Heptane: 5/17 at 21 % O2 vs 0/11 at 30–34 % O2; Methanol: 9/12 at 21 % O2 vs 2/13 at 30–34 % O2. Remaining tests ended in burnout ('completion') or droplet disruption. Limitation: Isolated droplets, two fuels; 'extinction' here means the flame went out before the droplet was consumed (often radiative), not the action of an extinguisher. Counts, not a model.

sources.title: Microgravity and 1-g rankings of materials can disagree
sources.text: In SAFFIRE-II, 4 of 4 silicone samples (0.27–1.03 mm) had a burn length of about 0 in microgravity at 20 cm/s, while 2 of the 4 matching 1-g reference burns were complete. Flames did spread in microgravity over: PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric). Limitation: One test per configuration; single flow speed and near-normal O2.
